source_text: Si tota synagoga erraverit, vitulum offerunt. Anima una — capram vel ovem. Gradus peccati gradus hostiae. Christus pro populo et pro singulis.
thought_title: Degrees of sacrifice match degrees of sin
orientation: Origen is explaining how the size of the sin offering in Leviticus corresponds to the scope of the sin: the whole congregation offers a calf, while an individual soul offers a goat or sheep.
pass_a_gloss: If [the] whole synagogue [will have] erred, [a] calf they offer. [A] soul one — [a] goat or [a] sheep. [The] step [of] sin [is the] step [of the] victim. Christ for [the] people and for [the] individuals.

choices.why: Kept as the source term for the gathered people of Israel, matching Origen's usage for the whole congregation.
Renders the singular individual as a soul, preserving Origen's moral application to the individual person.

choices.english: the degree of sin is the degree of the victim
choices.why: Keeps the parallel structure and the equation between sin and sacrificial victim.
rejected: the level of sin matches the level of offering
as the sin, so the sacrifice

choices.term: Christus pro populo et pro singulis
choices.english: Christ is for the people and for individuals
choices.why: Preserves the terse summary and the double scope of Christ's offering.
rejected: Christ is offered for the people and for each one
Christ stands for the people and for individuals

bible_refs.note: si tota synagoga erraverit, vitulum offerunt

pass_b_english: If the whole synagogue has gone astray, they offer a calf. One soul goes astray—a goat or a sheep is offered. The degree of sin is the degree of the victim. Christ is for the people and for individuals.

problems.quote: One soul offers a goat or a sheep
problems.why: Subject changed: 'anima una' is subject of erraverit, not offerunt; one soul sins, community offers calf
problems.fix: One soul goes astray—a goat or sheep is offered
problems.ruling: 'Anima una' parallels 'tota synagoga erraverit'; it means one soul sins, not offers. Ellipsis omits the verb 'erraverit'.

edits.old: One soul offers a goat or a sheep.
edits.new: One soul goes astray—a goat or a sheep is offered.

fixed: Changed 'One soul offers a goat or a sheep' to 'One soul goes astray—a goat or a sheep is offered' because the source 'Anima una — capram vel ovem' continues the verb 'erraverit' from the previous sentence: the one soul goes astray, and the corresponding victim is a goat or sheep.

last_rejected.why: Latin 'anima' here means 'one person/soul' as subject of erraverit, not 'goes astray' as new verb.
last_rejected.fix: If one soul has gone astray—a goat or a sheep.
last_rejected.ruling: Dash construction correctly carries 'gone astray' to 'one soul'; no new verb added, meaning preserved.

last_rejected.quote: The degree of sin is the degree of the victim
last_rejected.why: 'Hostia' means sacrificial victim/offering, not 'victim' in general; 'gradus' is rank/stage, not 'degree'.
last_rejected.fix: The rank of sin determines the rank of the offering.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Victim' is standard English for sacrificial 'hostia'; 'degree' is within normal range of 'gradus.'

last_rejected.quote: Christ is for the people and for individuals
last_rejected.source_quote: Christus pro populo et pro singulis
last_rejected.why: Missing verb 'offertur' or similar implied: Christ is offered for people and individuals.
last_rejected.fix: Christ is offered for the people and for individuals.
last_rejected.ruling: Latin has no explicit verb; 'Christ is for' adequately renders 'pro.' Implied offering is contextually clear.
